After D4, three dynamic capabilities are first-class in the graph engine and three workflow patterns become expressible as ordinary templates: (1) Conditional paths — an edge may carry a deterministic activation guard over its source context's captured D2 output, so a classifier context routes exactly the branches its verdict selects and untaken branches skip cleanly (Classify-And-Act). (2) Runtime graph expansion — an authorized running implementer appends a bounded subgraph (new contexts, tasks, edges, including edges into multiple pre-declared unstarted downstream consumers) through one idempotent command, so a generator fans out N candidate contexts converging on a planner-authored filter (Generate-And-Filter, dynamic fan-out). (3) General loops — a declared loop group repeats a single-entry/single-exit body of one or more contexts by cloning it into immutable per-pass instances until a designated exit context's captured output satisfies the exit predicate, with worker + independent-judge bodies working from the first slice (Loop-Until-Done). All control flow remains deterministic and engine-evaluated: agents supply judgment exclusively as typed structured outputs, and every routing, expansion, and loop decision is reconstructible from durable events.

invariants.statement: All structural mutation — agent expansion and engine loop unrolling alike — rides applyLiveExecutionEdits inside executionRepository.mutateActive under the loop-generation fence and the live-edit frontier invariant, with server-derived sources; never a second mutation path, never a bare repository write. The Kahn acyclicity check stays authoritative and continues to re-run on every accepted live edit. The completed context status stays terminal. One pure shared control-flow projection module owns guard resolution, skip propagation, active-dependency selection, and publish settlement; the scheduler, lane readiness, joins, upstream-input resolution, completion, final publish, CLI, and UI all derive from it and never re-implement route semantics. Guard documents are validated and evaluated exclusively through the single-source schema-subset module (validateJsonSchemaSubset and its exported descriptor) — no second evaluator; the module is soundness-sensitive (own-property access, adversarial fixtures). New config defaults are seeded only in SEEDED_WORKFLOW_DEFAULTS. Persisted-field discipline applies to every new field: repository mapping, maximal round-trip contract fixture (assertRoundTripDurability), migration/floor behavior, and blob-bounds declarations for blob-shaped fields. The task-completion loop and context validators stay first-class — loops are additive. Standard repo contract: red-green TDD, strict typing, no vi.mock for internal modules, typed event publication, bun run seams:check on boundary changes.

tasks.instructions:
Approved task dynamic-graph-primitives/T10

Failing tests first per behavior. Canonical-JSON SHA-256 hashing; idempotency on (sourceContextId, requestId): identical hash replays the permanent acceptance receipt, different hash refuses while the refusal record is retained, unknown (including ring-evicted) re-validates as a NEW attempt against current state. Enforce exact caps (5 contexts / 25 tasks / 40 edges / 64 KB per request; 10 per adding context; cumulative 25 expansion-created per execution excluding seed and loop clones). Refusals commit durable ring receipts plus typed refused events with no graph change and no liveRevision bump; acceptances persist permanent receipts with provenance. Round-trip fixtures for expansionReceipts against real SQLite.

Narrow context pack
Requirements:
- dynamic-graph-primitives/R6: A running implementer lane whose context resolves mutability.allowAgentContextAdd true shall append a bounded subgraph — new contexts with tasks, and edges — through one idempotent agent-facing command applied via the fenced prepare/finalize mutation staging without pausing the execution: every accepted request creates at least one new context; every new context is reachable from the invoker; every task in the payload targets a batch-created context; every edge source is the invoker or a batch-created node; every edge target is a batch-created node or one of multiple pre-declared rejoin contexts each individually downstream of the invoker, unstarted, and unreserved at finalize time; full validation runs during prepare with an O(payload) fenced finalize that re-verifies the definition fingerprint, liveRevision, envelope invariants, and absence of a pending halt; all-or-nothing; one liveRevision bump on acceptance and none on refusal.
- dynamic-graph-primitives/R8: Expansion shall be bounded and audited with exact ceilings: per request ≤5 contexts, ≤25 tasks, ≤40 edges, and ≤64 KB canonical payload; ≤10 contexts per adding context; a CUMULATIVE ≤25 expansion-created contexts per execution (seed contexts and loop-pass clones excluded). Refusals shall emit typed events and persist refusal receipts in a bounded ring of the 20 most recent per execution; an attempt whose refusal record has been evicted is re-validated as a new attempt against current state. Accepted expansions shall persist permanent receipts (initiator, rationale, added ids, payload hash) with node-level provenance, bounded by the cumulative cap; and the persistence blob-bounds contract shall declare every new field.
Approved decisions:
- dynamic-graph-primitives/D5: Prepare/finalize fenced by a repository-owned state revision; caps cumulative; eviction treated honestly
  Chosen approach: FENCE: the repository owns a monotonic executionStateRevision bumped by EVERY mutateActive commit (scheduler and runtime mutations included — liveRevision alone misses them). prepareLiveExecutionEdits captures it with the snapshot; finalizePreparedEdits splices the prepared whole-state ONLY when the stateRevision is unchanged; otherwise it re-applies the prepared OPS payload-locally onto the CURRENT execution with the cheap envelope recheck (validation evidence carries over from prepare; a frontier-relevant conflict triggers a full reprepare outside the lock). Concurrent scheduler/runtime writes can therefore never be erased by an install. CAPS: the 25-context execution cap is CUMULATIVE over expansion-created contexts — seed contexts and loop-pass clones are excluded (loop clones are governed by the pass backstop) — so removal never frees budget and the cap is monotone. EVICTION: an unknown (requestId, hash) — including one evicted from the refusal ring — is treated as a NEW attempt and re-validated from scratch; the design drops the unkeepable promise of identical re-refusal, and requestIds are documented single-use (reuse with a different payload after eviction is indistinguishable from a new request and is validated as one). Capability auth, ≥1-new-context admission, canonical hashing, deterministic ids, permanent acceptance receipts unchanged.
  Reason: The staging seam is safe under concurrency by construction, and every cap and idempotency promise is one persistence can actually keep.
- dynamic-graph-primitives/D12: The authoritative persisted-field inventory (supersedes every earlier partial listing)
  Chosen approach: This decision IS the inventory; R14.2 mirrors it and the persisted-blob-bounds contract test enumerates exactly these fields. DEFINITION TIER: edges[].id (required unique; legacy definitions normalized deterministically at load), edges[].when, contexts[].routing (cardinality), loopGroups[] (template with contexts/tasks/internal edges, entry/exit ids, until, maxPasses, resolved planRepair block, templateVersion). RUNTIME TIER: contextStates[].skipReason; contextStates[].landingIntent { baselineSha, laneId, worktreePath, mode: lane_commit | fan_in_merge | solo_commit, token, state: pending | landed | retry, receipts } persisted at DISPATCH (before the first agent turn); execution.routeSettlements[sourceContextId] { captureIteration, routeControlRevision, evaluations, cardinalityOutcome, at } (≤1 per source); execution.routeControlRevisions[sourceContextId] (monotonic); execution.loopStates[loopGroupId] { activation: pending | active | untaken | concluded, passCount, slotLedger: [{pass, state: reserved | counted | released}], loopControlRevision, boundaryInputs snapshot, latest LoopDecisionRecord per pass }; execution.expansionReceipts { accepted: permanent within the cumulative cap, refusals: 20-entry ring }. REMOVED/SUPERSEDED: the boolean commitStatus (landingIntent replaces it) and any append-only decision arrays in the blob (the events table holds full history; the blob holds latest markers only). All fields Zod-optional with floor defaults; one additive migration; repository mapping + codec + maximal round-trip fixtures + blob-bounds declarations for template, receipts, boundaryInputs, skipReason, landingIntent, and loopStates; storage.ts accept-time validation covers new authored fields.
  Reason: Persistence has exactly one authoritative declaration site, mirrored by the contract tests.
Acceptance criteria and required validation:
- dynamic-graph-primitives/R6.3: Retrying a request with the same source context, requestId, and canonical payload hash replays the prior acceptance receipt with no duplicate mutation (acceptance receipts permanent within the cumulative cap); the same requestId with a different hash is refused while the refusal record is retained; an unknown (requestId, hash) — including one evicted from the refusal ring — is treated as a NEW attempt and re-validated against current state (requestIds documented single-use); an accepted request that would create zero new contexts is refused.

  Approved strategy note: aligned with the D5 eviction contract — no identical-re-refusal promise
- dynamic-graph-primitives/R6.4: One expansion feeds multiple pre-declared rejoin contexts when each satisfies the per-target conditions (downstream of invoker, unstarted, unreserved — re-checked inside the serialized mutation); a batch with any failing rejoin target is refused whole.

tasks.instructions:
Approved task dynamic-graph-primitives/T11

Failing validation tests first for every refusal. Add loopGroups to both definition tiers (body template with contexts/tasks/internal edges, entry/exit ids, until, maxPasses, templateVersion, seed-resolved planRepair block). The accept-time resolver snapshots authored body contexts into the versioned template, removes them from executionContexts, and materializes pass 1 with reserved ids (<loopGroupId>__p<K>__… for contexts, tasks, AND edges; authored ids matching the reserved pattern refuse). Terminal-contract validation: exit declares outputSchema, until subset-valid and statically compatible. V1 restrictions refuse: nested/overlapping bodies, disconnected or multi-entry/exit bodies, external edges bypassing entry/exit, non-reconverging internal conditionals, loop declarations in expansion payloads, and expansion from inside an active body.

Narrow context pack
Requirements:
- dynamic-graph-primitives/R9: A seed-authored loop group shall repeat a connected single-entry/single-exit body of one or more contexts — with worker + independent-judge (multi-context) bodies supported from the first slice — by uniform immutable DAG unrolling with POST-LAND settlement: when a pass's exit instance has landed (completed, committed, lane-visible) or resolved skipped, one fenced settlement transaction evaluates the until predicate against the banked exit output and either concludes the loop, materializes the next pass (cloned from the versioned body template with reserved collision-proof ids for contexts, tasks, and edges), or halts; the settlement decision is idempotent on its durable decision record, an unconcluded loop's exit holds all external edges unresolved so downstream work cannot become eligible in the landed-but-unsettled window, and a completed-but-uncommitted exit is reconciled on resume via a durable commit intent before settlement proceeds. The loop terminal contract is validated at accept time: the exit context must declare an outputSchema and the until predicate must be subset-valid and statically compatible with it. Loop-boundary inputs are pinned via a durable activation-time snapshot — each pass's entry receives the snapshot plus the bounded Loop History (boundary routing edges are consumed once by the first pass and never cloned) — while ordinary upstream-input injection between same-pass body contexts is unchanged. Skip semantics distinguish an untaken loop (skips entirely with its body, no halt) from an active loop whose exit resolves skipped (typed loop_exit_skipped halt) or unevaluable (typed invariant halt). The graph remains acyclic and no completed context is reopened.
- dynamic-graph-primitives/R11: V1 loop composition shall be conservative: loop groups are seed-authored only (expansion payloads may not declare them); bodies are non-nested, non-overlapping, connected single-entry/single-exit subgraphs with external incoming edges targeting the entry and external outgoing edges originating at the exit; conditional branches inside a body must reconverge at the exit; runtime expansion from inside an active body is refused. Pass instances clone from a versioned body template owned by the loop declaration: template membership (which contexts form the body, entry, exit) freezes once the first pass starts; template content (context prose, acceptance criteria, and tasks) is editable only while the execution is paused or halted, each edit bumping the template version, and every pass records the template version it cloned; completed pass instances are never edited. The exit predicate is amendable only while the execution is halted (operator live edit or plan repair, each with a required rationale); raising maxPasses is the only other edit admitted on a started loop.
Approved decisions:
- dynamic-graph-primitives/D7: Durable slot ledger with definition-order arbitration; pass 1 reserves at activation; provisioning failures release and halt recoverably
  Chosen approach: The backstop protocol is a durable slotLedger in loopStates: entries {pass, state: reserved | counted | released}. PASS 1 reserves its slot in the same mutation that marks the loop active (external activation resolved) — before any pass-1 instance becomes eligible; later passes reserve inside their settlement transaction before cloning, exactly as revision 7. Arbitration is durable and deterministic: within one scheduling mutation, loop groups are processed in definition order and the ledger records the grant order, so a restart replays identical arbitration; when no slot remains, activation or settlement halts scope execution without materializing. Provisioning failure releases the reservation durably and routes through the existing provisioning-failure halt path with the materialized pass instances halted-recoverable (resume retries provisioning and re-reserves; released slots are reusable). Logical exit mapping, activation states, boundary-input snapshot, reserved id patterns, and first-running counting are unchanged.
  Reason: Every pass — including the first — is admitted through one durable, ordered, restart-replayable protocol.

- dynamic-graph-primitives/R9.5: Accept-time validation refuses a loop whose exit context declares no outputSchema or whose until predicate is subset-invalid or statically incompatible with the exit schema, alongside the v1 body-shape refusals. (Runtime terminal behavior is covered by R9.6; entry-input injection by R16.1.)

tasks.title: dynamic-graph-primitives/T12 Loop settlement: activation, logical exit, slot ledger, and the decision transaction
tasks.instructions:
Approved task dynamic-graph-primitives/T12

Engine work under red-green with the worker+judge shape as the primary fixture. The loop terminal contract is validated at accept time: the exit context must declare an outputSchema and the until predicate must be subset-valid and statically compatible with it. Loop-boundary inputs are pinned via a durable activation-time snapshot — each pass's entry receives the snapshot plus the bounded Loop History (boundary routing edges are consumed once by the first pass and never cloned) — while ordinary upstream-input injection between same-pass body contexts is unchanged. Skip semantics distinguish an untaken loop (skips entirely with its body, no halt) from an active loop whose exit resolves skipped (typed loop_exit_skipped halt) or unevaluable (typed invariant halt). The graph remains acyclic and no completed context is reopened.
- dynamic-graph-primitives/R16: The engine shall maintain a per-loop ledger with bounded current state and complete durable history: the execution record retains bounded markers — activation state, pass count and reservations, the boundary-input snapshot, and the latest authoritative LoopDecisionRecord per pass (carrying the full deduplication key: loop, pass, loopControlRevision, exit-capture identity, template version, verdict, outcome) — while the complete decision history, including repeated re-decisions of one pass under amended control revisions, is durably recorded in the append-only event log; inspector and CLI ledger views derive from both. Approved decisions:
- dynamic-graph-primitives/D8: Landing lifecycle: mode-specific intent persisted at dispatch; settlement waits on reconciled landings
  Chosen approach: The landingIntent is persisted when the context is DISPATCHED — the same mutation that assigns its lane records { baselineSha (the lane head at assignment, currently runner-local preTurnLaneHeadSha), laneId, worktreePath, mode, token, state: pending } — so no landing evidence ever exists only in memory. tasks.title: dynamic-graph-primitives/T23 Planner-facing docs and the documented handoff convention
tasks.instructions:
Approved task dynamic-graph-primitives/T23

Deliver the documentation R16.3 requires: the graph-workflow-planning skill gains guards/cardinality/else authoring, loop groups with worker+judge bodies, expansion authoring incl. half-static Generate-And-Filter and the caps, and the handoff-field outputSchema convention with a worked example; .kiro/steering/workflows.md gains the new config blocks in the cascade table, adoption-matrix rows for the projection/expansion/settlement modules, staging-seam notes, and seeded defaults incl. mutability.allowAgentContextAdd; CLI help-registry entries for the new verbs. Verify every referenced schema field and CLI verb exists at the tip; update AGENTS.md only if a command or canonical boundary changed.

Narrow context pack
Requirements:
- dynamic-graph-primitives/R16: The engine shall maintain a per-loop ledger with bounded current state and complete durable history: the execution record retains bounded markers — activation state, pass count and reservations, the boundary-input snapshot, and the latest authoritative LoopDecisionRecord per pass (carrying the full deduplication key: loop, pass, loopControlRevision, exit-capture identity, template version, verdict, outcome) — while the complete decision history, including repeated re-decisions of one pass under amended control revisions, is durably recorded in the append-only event log; inspector and CLI ledger views derive from both. A bounded Loop History section (most-recent-N passes, size-capped) is injected into each pass's ENTRY prompt only; same-pass body contexts receive ordinary upstream injection. The ledger introduces no new mutable state and no new communication channel; free-form inter-pass narrative is schema-carried via a documented handoff-field convention for body outputSchemas in the planner skill.
- dynamic-graph-primitives/R13: D4 shall ship full read-side legibility with structural writes remaining CLI-only: the graph page and inspector render conditional edges with their guards, skipped nodes with recorded reasons, loop groups with pass badges and budgets, and runtime-added nodes with provenance; the CLI live outline reports the same. Every D4 CONDITIONAL decision — guarded-edge resolution, skip, cardinality halt, expansion acceptance and refusal, loop decision — persists an authoritative durable decision record (typed events and execution state) from which UI and CLI views derive; unconditional-edge scheduling emits no new events, so pre-D4 executions' event sequences are unchanged.
- dynamic-graph-primitives/R7: Expansion authority shall be a per-context cascaded mutability flag seeded default-off, exercisable only by the bound implementer, authenticated by a signed lane capability scoped to the execution, context, conversation, and implementer lane and re-verified inside the serialized mutation. Generated contexts may carry agent-authored prose, acceptance criteria, tasks, a subset-valid outputSchema, and tuning overrides — implementer, iterationPolicy, circuitBreaker, and scriptValidator, the last MONOTONIC (enable-only; an override or seed that would disable an inherited-enabled script validator is refused). Protected blocks — contextValidator, humanApprovalGate, askUserQuestions, collaboration, planRepair, mutability — derive from the INVOKER's resolved config regardless of configFromContextId and refuse payload overrides, so no expansion path weakens a child's validation or approval gates. Expansion authority shall resolve disabled on every generated child after config inheritance from any source, preserving sibling mutability fields; and a generated context with zero tasks shall be refused.
Approved decisions:
- dynamic-graph-primitives/D9: Ledger views read blob markers plus a shared cursor-paginated event reader
  Chosen approach: History access gets a real reader: a shared cursor-paginated events reader (seq-keyed, ascending or descending, bounded page size) over the graph_workflow_events table, used by the inspector ledger view, the CLI ledger/outline surfaces, and tests — the existing events endpoint exposes only a bounded tail, which cannot serve full decision history. Current state comes from the blob markers (loopStates, routeSettlements, receipts). Loop History prompt injection is ENTRY-ONLY, bounded (3 passes / 2 KB per context / 16 KB per section), sourced from the blob markers and pass-instance captures — never from the paginated reader (prompts need recent, not full, history). The handoff-field outputSchema convention is documented in the planner skill in the same change.
  Reason: Complete history is reachable through one shared reader while prompts and reducers keep reading bounded current state.
- dynamic-graph-primitives/D5: Prepare/finalize fenced by a repository-owned state revision; caps cumulative; eviction treated honestly
  Chosen approach: FENCE: the repository owns a monotonic executionStateRevision bumped by EVERY mutateActive commit (scheduler and runtime mutations included — liveRevision alone misses them). prepareLiveExecutionEdits captures it with the snapshot; finalizePreparedEdits splices the prepared whole-state ONLY when the stateRevision is unchanged; otherwise it re-applies the prepared OPS payload-locally onto the CURRENT execution with the cheap envelope recheck (validation evidence carries over from prepare; a frontier-relevant conflict triggers a full reprepare outside the lock). Concurrent scheduler/runtime writes can therefore never be erased by an install. CAPS: the 25-context execution cap is CUMULATIVE over expansion-created contexts — seed contexts and loop-pass clones are excluded (loop clones are governed by the pass backstop) — so removal never frees budget and the cap is monotone. EVICTION: an unknown (requestId, hash) — including one evicted from the refusal ring — is treated as a NEW attempt and re-validated from scratch; the design drops the unkeepable promise of identical re-refusal, and requestIds are documented single-use (reuse with a different payload after eviction is indistinguishable from a new request and is validated as one). Capability auth, ≥1-new-context admission, canonical hashing, deterministic ids, permanent acceptance receipts unchanged.
  Reason: The staging seam is safe under concurrency by construction, and every cap and idempotency promise is one persistence can actually keep.
Acceptance criteria and required validation:
- dynamic-graph-primitives/R16.3: The graph-workflow-planning skill documents the handoff-field outputSchema convention with a worked example, plus guard/cardinality/else authoring, loop groups with worker+judge bodies, and expansion authoring with the caps; .kiro/steering/workflows.md carries the new config blocks, adoption-matrix rows, and seeded defaults; every schema field name and CLI verb referenced exists at the tip.
  Required evidence: validator_verdict
  Approved strategy note: doc-accuracy verification against the shipped schemas and CLI

tasks.title: dynamic-graph-primitives/T3 Extract the output lookup and build the pure route-projection module
tasks.instructions:
Approved task dynamic-graph-primitives/T3

Two steps, one coherent module boundary. FIRST extract the raw four-state output lookup from context-outputs.ts into dependency-free output-lookup.ts (characterization tests pin behavior; context-outputs re-exports its public API byte-compatibly; existing tests stay green unmodified). THEN build route-projection.ts over it: per-edge resolution with guard evaluation via validateJsonSchemaSubset (matching activates, non-matching deactivates, non-captured lookups never evaluate — adversarial fixtures for __proto__/constructor/exotic keys), order-free else resolution, cardinality outcomes, the uniform conjunctive readiness rule, recursive skip derivation, the transitive must-run set, publish settlement, logical/effective loop-exit resolution (activation-state aware), and projection-resolved edges carrying logicalSourceId + effectiveSourceId. Unit-test the full truth table red-green including the mixed-input counterexample and the skipped-intermediate fan-in topology. Pure, browser-safe.

Narrow context pack
Requirements:
- dynamic-graph-primitives/R2: The engine shall resolve routes deterministically under one uniform rule: a context becomes eligible when every incoming edge is satisfied, where an unconditional edge is satisfied when its source lands (and is omitted when its source is skipped) and a conditional edge is satisfied when its guard evaluates true over the completed source's captured output — conditional edges are not a special veto class; all drawn edges are conjunctive prerequisites. Guard evaluation gates only the routing decision; target eligibility additionally honors the existing land-gate: a satisfied edge schedules its target only once the source's work is committed and lane-visible, and a source whose fan-in merge is pending or failed blocks (never skips) its dependents until the merge resolves or the execution halts. Guards resolve only after the source context completes; a guard whose source is skipped resolves false; a resolved-false guard skips the target; when every predecessor path is skipped, a fan-in skips recursively. A completed conditional source with an unevaluable output (pending, none, or orphaned) produces a typed resumable invariant halt whose sanctioned remedy is a quiescent live edit of the unstarted target's incoming edges (amend or remove the guard, or reroute), followed by resume — never a false evaluation, and never an edit to the completed source.
- dynamic-graph-primitives/R1: An execution-context edge shall optionally carry a source-local activation guard — either a D2 schema-subset document the source context's captured output must match, or an else marker — validated at accept time: a guard-bearing edge requires its source to declare an outputSchema, the guard document must itself satisfy the schema subset, and at most one else edge is admitted per source context.
- dynamic-graph-primitives/R3: Outgoing conditional matches from one source shall be independent by default (zero, one, or many branches may activate), with an optional per-source cardinality policy (atLeastOne or exactlyOne) that turns under- or over-selection into a typed resumable routing halt; an activated else edge counts toward cardinality, so a source with an else edge always satisfies atLeastOne and violates exactlyOne only on multiple activations; an authoring warning fires when a closed-enum guard field leaves values uncovered with no else edge; first-match-wins ordering shall not exist.
Approved decisions:
- dynamic-graph-primitives/D1: Projection exports logical and effective edge sources; every consumer migrates to projection-resolved edges
  Chosen approach: Projection-resolved edges carry BOTH ids: logicalSourceId (the authored source — for a loop's external edges, the declared exitContextId) and effectiveSourceId (the context instance whose landed work and capture actually satisfy the edge — the concluding pass's exit instance for concluded loops; null while unresolved). The design names the consumer migration explicitly, because every current consumer reads edge.sourceContextId raw: the scheduler's prerequisite map, lane visibility (isUpstreamVisibleToDownstream and reachable-lane math), join source-lane planning, and upstream-input/prompt resolution all switch to projection-resolved edges and MUST use effectiveSourceId for landing, visibility, and data; UI/CLI render the logical id with the effective id as provenance. A lint (arch test) forbids new direct reads of edge.sourceContextId outside the projection and the validation module. Layered output lookup, loop-exit gating, and activation-aware resolution are unchanged from revision 7.
  Reason: The logical exit stays immutable in authored topology while every runtime consumer is pointed, checkably, at the instance that really satisfies the edge.
- dynamic-graph-primitives/D2: Legacy edge ids normalize deterministically; the routeControlRevision bump set is closed; guard design unchanged
  Chosen approach: COMPATIBILITY: launching or loading a legacy definition with absent or duplicate edge ids does not refuse — ids are normalized deterministically with the existing mintLiveEdgeId scheme (src__tgt, then -2, -3 by duplicate ordinal) at inflate time, identically on every load, and saved-tier writes persist the normalized ids; uniqueness is enforced for NEW authoring. BUMP SET (closed list): a source's routeControlRevision bumps on add-edge, update-edge, or remove-edge touching any of its outgoing conditional edges (including else edges), a change to its routing.cardinality, an expansion adding a guarded edge from it, and a template edit altering guarded edges inside a loop body it sources. Nothing else bumps it. Guard wrapper, subset evaluation, compatibility lint, and id-addressed edits are unchanged from revision 7.
  Reason: Identity becomes strict for new work without breaking old work, and the revision that keys settlement has a testably complete trigger list.
Acceptance criteria and required validation:
- dynamic-graph-primitives/R1.2: Guard evaluation uses the shared schema-subset validator: a captured source output matching the guard document activates the edge and a non-matching output deactivates it, with pending/orphaned/none lookups never evaluating — proven at the projection level with adversarial fixtures (__proto__, constructor, exotic keys). (Durable recording of evaluations is covered by R13.3.)
  Required evidence: test_run
  Approved strategy note: No additional strategy note was approved.
- dynamic-graph-primitives/R1.3: At runtime an else edge activates exactly when no conditional sibling edge from the same source activated, independent of edge declaration order.
  Required evidence: test_run
  Approved strategy note: No additional strategy note was approved.
- dynamic-graph-primitives/R2.1: A target with one landed unconditional dependency and one resolved-false conditional guard is skipped, not run — pinning the uniform rule that every drawn edge is a conjunctive prerequisite and a sibling edge's satisfaction cannot override an unsatisfied guard.
  Required evidence: test_run
  Approved strategy note: the mixed-input counterexample from the design negotiation; the any-active alternative makes guards advisory in mixed shapes
- dynamic-graph-primitives/R2.3: Skip propagation and fan-in compose by topology: a fan-in whose incoming edges are unconditional but sourced from branch contexts (one skipped intermediate, one landed) runs on the landed branch with the skipped source's edge omitted; a target carrying a direct resolved-false guard skips regardless of its other satisfied edges (R2.1); when every predecessor path of a fan-in is skipped, the fan-in and its exclusive descendants skip recursively; the fan-in always waits for every incoming route to resolve first.
  Required evidence: test_run
  Approved strategy note: pins the omitted-edge-from-skipped-intermediate topology that reconciles R2.1 with single-active-branch fan-ins

tasks.title: dynamic-graph-primitives/T4 The skipped context status lifecycle
tasks.instructions:
Approved task dynamic-graph-primitives/T4

Failing transition-table tests first. Add "skipped" to graphWorkflowContextStatusSchema and CONTEXT_STATUS_TRANSITIONS (pending → skipped, ready → skipped, skipped terminal); transitions only via transitionContextStatus with contextState.skipReason persisted in the same mutation and the graph-workflow-context-skipped event emitted. resetContextStateToInitial throws on skipped. getContextOutput gains the fifth public lookup kind { kind: "skipped" } composed in context-outputs (not the raw lookup); buildUpstreamInputsSection renders skipped predecessors as branch-not-taken. Repository mapping + round-trip fixture updates for skipReason ride along.

Narrow context pack
Requirements:
- dynamic-graph-primitives/R4: A skipped context shall be a first-class terminal, frozen status: it holds no lane, owes no task, validator, approval, or output debt, contributes no merge input, records the guard verdicts that skipped it, is exempt from the completion invariant and final-publish preconditions, and is irreversible within the execution — no transition leaves skipped and reset-context refuses it.
Approved decisions:
- dynamic-graph-primitives/D3: skipped as a first-class terminal context status with persisted reason
  Chosen approach: Add "skipped" to graphWorkflowContextStatusSchema and CONTEXT_STATUS_TRANSITIONS (pending → skipped, ready → skipped; skipped → [] terminal); transitions happen only via transitionContextStatus inside the scheduling mutation, with the evaluated guard verdicts persisted as contextState.skipReason { edgeEvaluations: [{edgeId, verdict}], at } and a graph-workflow-context-skipped event. Exemptions wired through the projection: findContextsWithUnfinishedTasks, the output-debt sweep (contextOwesOutput loop), planFinalPublishJoin, getEligibleContextIds, and join source-lane math all treat skipped as settled-with-nothing. getContextOutput gains a fifth lookup kind { kind: "skipped" }; buildUpstreamInputsSection renders skipped predecessors as 'branch not taken'. resetContextStateToInitial throws on skipped (irreversibility lock).
  Reason: R4's ripple has a dozen named consumers; a real status plus one projection is the only shape where a missed consumer is a compile/test failure rather than a stranded frontier.

  Required evidence: test_run
  Approved strategy note: No additional strategy note was approved.

  Required evidence: test_run

tasks.title: dynamic-graph-primitives/T5 Wire routing into the scheduler: settlements, landing intents, halts, and the consumer migration
tasks.instructions:
Approved task dynamic-graph-primitives/T5

Engine integration under red-green: wire the route projection into getEligibleContextIds, classifyContextSchedulability, join planning, the completion invariant, and final-publish quiescence; migrate every consumer of edge.sourceContextId to projection-resolved edges (effectiveSourceId for landing/visibility/data) with the arch lint. Persist landingIntent at dispatch with mode-specific evidence and THE ACTUAL COMMITTERS integrated: the server-side lane committer (lane-committer.ts) and solo committer embed the deterministic token; self-authored lane commits adopted at head-advance gain verifiable evidence via the recorded baseline→head SHA range in the intent receipts; fan-in merges reconcile against join records. Reconciliation at resume/normalization; route settlement waits on landed intents (merge-pending/failed blocks, never skips). Write routeSettlements exact-once keyed (source, captureIteration, routeControlRevision) with the route-resolved event in the same mutation; add the routing_cardinality and routing_invariant halt variants with the quiescent edge-edit remedy proven. Prove skip ripple end-to-end: executions with skipped contexts complete, final publish excludes them, restart preserves persisted skips.

Narrow context pack
Requirements:
- dynamic-graph-primitives/R2: The engine shall resolve routes deterministically under one uniform rule: a context becomes eligible when every incoming edge is satisfied, where an unconditional edge is satisfied when its source lands (and is omitted when its source is skipped) and a conditional edge is satisfied when its guard evaluates true over the completed source's captured output — conditional edges are not a special veto class; all drawn edges are conjunctive prerequisites. Guard evaluation gates only the routing decision; target eligibility additionally honors the existing land-gate: a satisfied edge schedules its target only once the source's work is committed and lane-visible, and a source whose fan-in merge is pending or failed blocks (never skips) its dependents until the merge resolves or the execution halts. Guards resolve only after the source context completes; a guard whose source is skipped resolves false; a resolved-false guard skips the target; when every predecessor path is skipped, a fan-in skips recursively. A completed conditional source with an unevaluable output (pending, none, or orphaned) produces a typed resumable invariant halt whose sanctioned remedy is a quiescent live edit of the unstarted target's incoming edges (amend or remove the guard, or reroute), followed by resume — never a false evaluation, and never an edit to the completed source.
- dynamic-graph-primitives/R4: A skipped context shall be a first-class terminal, frozen status: it holds no lane, owes no task, validator, approval, or output debt, contributes no merge input, records the guard verdicts that skipped it, is exempt from the completion invariant and final-publish preconditions, and is irreversible within the execution — no transition leaves skipped and reset-context refuses it.
- dynamic-graph-primitives/R3: Outgoing conditional matches from one source shall be independent by default (zero, one, or many branches may activate), with an optional per-source cardinality policy (atLeastOne or exactlyOne) that turns under- or over-selection into a typed resumable routing halt; an activated else edge counts toward cardinality, so a source with an else edge always satisfies atLeastOne and violates exactlyOne only on multiple activations; an authoring warning fires when a closed-enum guard field leaves values uncovered with no else edge; first-match-wins ordering shall not exist.
Approved decisions:
- dynamic-graph-primitives/D1: Projection exports logical and effective edge sources; every consumer migrates to projection-resolved edges
  Chosen approach: Projection-resolved edges carry BOTH ids: logicalSourceId (the authored source — for a loop's external edges, the declared exitContextId) and effectiveSourceId (the context instance whose landed work and capture actually satisfy the edge — the concluding pass's exit instance for concluded loops; null while unresolved). The design names the consumer migration explicitly, because every current consumer reads edge.sourceContextId raw: the scheduler's prerequisite map, lane visibility (isUpstreamVisibleToDownstream and reachable-lane math), join source-lane planning, and upstream-input/prompt resolution all switch to projection-resolved edges and MUST use effectiveSourceId for landing, visibility, and data; UI/CLI render the logical id with the effective id as provenance. A lint (arch test) forbids new direct reads of edge.sourceContextId outside the projection and the validation module. Layered output lookup, loop-exit gating, and activation-aware resolution are unchanged from revision 7.
  Reason: The logical exit stays immutable in authored topology while every runtime consumer is pointed, checkably, at the instance that really satisfies the edge.
- dynamic-graph-primitives/D4: Bounded current markers in the blob; the full decision ledger lives in the events table
  Chosen approach: The execution blob retains only BOUNDED current markers: routeSettlements (≤ one per source, keyed by routeControlRevision), loopStates with the latest LoopDecisionRecord per pass plus counters/reservations, receipts within their caps. The FULL decision ledger — every route resolution, skip, expansion acceptance/refusal, and every loop decision including repeated re-decisions of one pass under amended control revisions — lives in the graph_workflow_events table, which is already append-only, unbounded by design, and durable; UI/CLI ledger views read events for history and the blob for current state. This resolves the contradiction where append-only decision arrays in the blob were not actually bounded by the 25-pass cap (one pass can be amended and re-decided repeatedly). Halt variants and event kinds are unchanged from revision 6; every event payload embeds the same record types the blob uses (LoopDecisionRecord, route settlement record).
  Reason: Current state stays small and provably bounded; history stays complete where history already lives.
- dynamic-graph-primitives/D8: Landing lifecycle: mode-specific intent persisted at dispatch; settlement waits on reconciled landings
  Chosen approach: The landingIntent is persisted when the context is DISPATCHED — the same mutation that assigns its lane records { baselineSha (the lane head at assignment, currently runner-local preTurnLaneHeadSha), laneId, worktreePath, mode, token, state: pending } — so no landing evidence ever exists only in memory. Modes carry mode-specific replayable evidence: lane_commit and solo_commit embed the deterministic token in the commit message (reconciliation probes the branch for token/SHA); fan_in_merge reconciles against the join's own durable merge records; approval-gated contexts keep the intent pending until approval resolves, then land normally. Reconciliation runs at resume/normalization and marks intents landed or retry; route and loop settlement treat only landed as satisfied. The remainder of settlement is unchanged from revision 7: projection-gated eligibility, LoopDecisionRecord as the idempotent done-marker keyed (loopGroupId, pass, loopControlRevision, exitCaptureIteration), prepare/finalize staging, resume re-decision under amended control revisions.
  Reason: Every landing mode leaves durable, replayable evidence from before the first turn, so restart classification never guesses.
Acceptance criteria and required validation:
- dynamic-graph-primitives/R2.2: A conditional edge does not resolve while its source holds a captured output but is not completed (e.g. parked on a human approval gate); an approval rejection that deletes the capture leaves the route unresolved rather than latched.
  Required evidence: test_run
  Approved strategy note: No additional strategy note was approved.
- dynamic-graph-primitives/R2.4: A completed conditional source observed with a pending, none, or orphaned output lookup halts the execution with a typed resumable invariant halt.
  Required evidence: test_run
  Approved strategy note: defense-in-depth: state should be unreachable under completion gating + frozen frontier
- dynamic-graph-primitives/R2.5: A conditional target does not become eligible while its completed source's work is uncommitted or not lane-visible, and a source with a pending or failed fan-in merge blocks its dependents (existing merge-retry and halt semantics) rather than activating or skipping them.
  Required evidence: test_run

tasks.instructions:
Approved task dynamic-graph-primitives/T6

Failing tests first. Implement the scoped enum-coverage authoring warning (single top-level enum/const guards only). tasks.title: dynamic-graph-primitives/T7 executionStateRevision and the prepare/finalize mutation staging seam
tasks.instructions:
Approved task dynamic-graph-primitives/T7

Red-green at the repository seam. Add the repository-owned monotonic executionStateRevision bumped by EVERY mutateActive commit. Split the pure live-edit core into prepareLiveExecutionEdits (clone, apply, full frontier validation outside any lock) and finalizePreparedEdits (O(payload) under the fence: splice on unchanged stateRevision, payload-local re-apply otherwise, reprepare signal on frontier conflicts, refusal under pendingHaltReason). Prove the fence with interleaving tests: scheduler and runtime mutations between prepare and finalize are never erased; existing live-edit behavior unchanged. Runs second in the runtime-edits.ts mutation-seam sequence after the guard-schema task.

Narrow context pack
Requirements:
- dynamic-graph-primitives/R6: A running implementer lane whose context resolves mutability.allowAgentContextAdd true shall append a bounded subgraph — new contexts with tasks, and edges — through one idempotent agent-facing command applied via the fenced prepare/finalize mutation staging without pausing the execution: every accepted request creates at least one new context; every new context is reachable from the invoker; every task in the payload targets a batch-created context; every edge source is the invoker or a batch-created node; every edge target is a batch-created node or one of multiple pre-declared rejoin contexts each individually downstream of the invoker, unstarted, and unreserved at finalize time; full validation runs during prepare with an O(payload) fenced finalize that re-verifies the definition fingerprint, liveRevision, envelope invariants, and absence of a pending halt; all-or-nothing; one liveRevision bump on acceptance and none on refusal.
- dynamic-graph-primitives/R14: D4 shall be additive and dormant-by-default: definitions and persisted executions absent D4 fields shall parse as unconditional edges, no loops, and expansion disabled, and shall execute with observational equivalence to pre-D4 behavior — identical scheduling decisions, context status transitions, and typed event sequences modulo timestamps and generated identifiers; and every new persisted field shall be covered by its repository mapping, the maximal round-trip contract fixtures, migration/floor behavior, and blob-bounds declarations.
- dynamic-graph-primitives/R9: A seed-authored loop group shall repeat a connected single-entry/single-exit body of one or more contexts — with worker + independent-judge (multi-context) bodies supported from the first slice — by uniform immutable DAG unrolling with POST-LAND settlement: when a pass's exit instance has landed (completed, committed, lane-visible) or resolved skipped, one fenced settlement transaction evaluates the until predicate against the banked exit output and either concludes the loop, materializes the next pass (cloned from the versioned body template with reserved collision-proof ids for contexts, tasks, and edges), or halts; the settlement decision is idempotent on its durable decision record, an unconcluded loop's exit holds all external edges unresolved so downstream work cannot become eligible in the landed-but-unsettled window, and a completed-but-uncommitted exit is reconciled on resume via a durable commit intent before settlement proceeds. The loop terminal contract is validated at accept time: the exit context must declare an outputSchema and the until predicate must be subset-valid and statically compatible with it. Loop-boundary inputs are pinned via a durable activation-time snapshot — each pass's entry receives the snapshot plus the bounded Loop History (boundary routing edges are consumed once by the first pass and never cloned) — while ordinary upstream-input injection between same-pass body contexts is unchanged. Skip semantics distinguish an untaken loop (skips entirely with its body, no halt) from an active loop whose exit resolves skipped (typed loop_exit_skipped halt) or unevaluable (typed invariant halt). The graph remains acyclic and no completed context is reopened.
Approved decisions:
- dynamic-graph-primitives/D5: Prepare/finalize fenced by a repository-owned state revision; caps cumulative; eviction treated honestly
  Chosen approach: FENCE: the repository owns a monotonic executionStateRevision bumped by EVERY mutateActive commit (scheduler and runtime mutations included — liveRevision alone misses them). prepareLiveExecutionEdits captures it with the snapshot; finalizePreparedEdits splices the prepared whole-state ONLY when the stateRevision is unchanged; otherwise it re-applies the prepared OPS payload-locally onto the CURRENT execution with the cheap envelope recheck (validation evidence carries over from prepare; a frontier-relevant conflict triggers a full reprepare outside the lock). Concurrent scheduler/runtime writes can therefore never be erased by an install. CAPS: the 25-context execution cap is CUMULATIVE over expansion-created contexts — seed contexts and loop-pass clones are excluded (loop clones are governed by the pass backstop) — so removal never frees budget and the cap is monotone. EVICTION: an unknown (requestId, hash) — including one evicted from the refusal ring — is treated as a NEW attempt and re-validated from scratch; the design drops the unkeepable promise of identical re-refusal, and requestIds are documented single-use (reuse with a different payload after eviction is indistinguishable from a new request and is validated as one). Capability auth, ≥1-new-context admission, canonical hashing, deterministic ids, permanent acceptance receipts unchanged.
  Reason: The staging seam is safe under concurrency by construction, and every cap and idempotency promise is one persistence can actually keep.
- dynamic-graph-primitives/D8: Landing lifecycle: mode-specific intent persisted at dispatch; settlement waits on reconciled landings
  Chosen approach: The landingIntent is persisted when the context is DISPATCHED — the same mutation that assigns its lane records { baselineSha (the lane head at assignment, currently runner-local preTurnLaneHeadSha), laneId, worktreePath, mode, token, state: pending } — so no landing evidence ever exists only in memory. Modes carry mode-specific replayable evidence: lane_commit and solo_commit embed the deterministic token in the commit message (reconciliation probes the branch for token/SHA); fan_in_merge reconciles against the join's own durable merge records; approval-gated contexts keep the intent pending until approval resolves, then land normally. Reconciliation runs at resume/normalization and marks intents landed or retry; route and loop settlement treat only landed as satisfied. The remainder of settlement is unchanged from revision 7: projection-gated eligibility, LoopDecisionRecord as the idempotent done-marker keyed (loopGroupId, pass, loopControlRevision, exitCaptureIteration), prepare/finalize staging, resume re-decision under amended control revisions.
  Reason: Every landing mode leaves durable, replayable evidence from before the first turn, so restart classification never guesses.
Acceptance criteria and required validation:
- dynamic-graph-primitives/R6.6: The prepare/finalize staging seam is fenced by the repository-owned executionStateRevision bumped on every mutateActive commit: a scheduler or runtime mutation interleaved between prepare and finalize is never erased — finalize splices only on an unchanged revision, re-applies ops payload-locally otherwise, and signals reprepare on frontier-relevant conflicts; finalize refuses under a pendingHaltReason.
  Required evidence: test_run
  Approved strategy note: interleaving tests at the seam; consumed by expansion and loop settlement
